public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI-powered search engines do not have consistent results, and Google's Bard AI and Bing AI made obvious errors in their first demos, which, from what the author can tell, happened largely because they make their best guess every time.

statement.excerpt: The problem with these AI-powered search engines is that they do not have consistent results. Both Google’s Bard AI and Bing AI had obvious errors in their first demos, largely in part because they are, from what I can tell, making their best guess every time.

from_speaker: Both Google’s Bard AI and Bing AI
obvious errors in their first demos
making their best guess every time
our_interpretation: Assess the full compound claim, retaining the proposed cause rather than scoring only the demo errors.
First demos means the initial February 2023 public promotional demonstrations, including Google's Bard advertisement.
The plain reading of inconsistent results is unreliable factual accuracy; it need not mean identical prompts must produce identical wording.
Best guess means probabilistic generation without assured factual correctness. Largely requires evidence that this mechanism substantially explains the particular errors.
From what I can tell qualifies confidence; it is not a condition that must occur.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish factual errors in both initial demonstrations and evidence connects unreliable accuracy chiefly to the proposed generation mechanism.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records disprove the alleged demo errors or controlled analysis establishes that the proposed mechanism did not substantially cause them.
